question: What includes information that should be located on the MAR? A. Medication dose B. Client’s next of kin C. Medication side effects D. Agency medication administration policies

When should a Medication Aide report a medication error to the supervisor? A. Before the next medication is due B. During the end-of-shift report C. As soon as the error occurs D. After calling the physician
What is one teaspoon of an elixir equal to? A. 10 milliliters B. 5 milliliters C. 1 ounce D. 1 pint
Which of the following is a symptom of anaphylaxis, a life-threatening allergic reaction? A. High blood pressure B. Quiet breathing C. Slow heart rate D. Wheezing
What should be the site selected for applying a transdermal patch? A. Cold B. Warm C. Hairless D. Odor free

Why is it important for you as a Medication Aide to introduce yourself to the residents? A. For the residents to know who is in charge B. To build relationships with the residents C. For the residents to be able to call you if needed D. To adhere to proper etiquette

You are asked by the Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) to give a resident his pain medication. You know your responsibility as the Medication Aide is to see that this request is followed up. Who should give further clarification? A. The resident B. Another CNA C. The manager D. The resident’s roommate

Which of the following actions may the MA complete appropriately? A. Administering medications B. Ordering medications C. Assessment of the resident’s condition D. Evaluating the effectiveness of medications

The Medication Aide is responsible for administering __________. A. Only the medications learned in school B. Medications under the direct supervision of a nurse C. Medications by all routes D. Expired medications
Before giving a medication, the label is checked for all of the following except __________. A. Dosage B. Expiration date C. Name D. Cost
There are six “rights” of medication administration. They include all the following except for __________. A. Right dose B. Right medication C. Right patient D. Right place E. Right time

A fellow Medication Aide going on break hands you a crushed pill and asks you to administer it to a resident. Which of the following responses is required from you as an MA? A. To give the medication right away B. To ask your fellow Medication Aide what the medication is and to administer it if it is the correct medication C. To politely refuse to do the other Medication Aide’s work and to let him or her give the medication when he or she returns from break D. To refuse to give the medication because it cannot be properly identified
“Give ibuprofen for pain every 6 hours as needed.” What component of this physician order is missing? A. The route B. The dose C. The frequency D. The condition

The Medication Aide is preparing to administer morning medications to residents. What is one important safety rule? A. Never leave an unattended cart unlocked. B. Always make sure that all medications are out of sight of other residents. C. Provide liquids to swallow medications. D. Check to make sure that the medication carts have charts available to make corrections as needed.

Storing medications is an important responsibility for the medication aide. Which of the following actions demonstrates the correct storing of a medication? A. Medications with similar names are stored close together. B. Mr. and Mrs. Jones’s medications are in the same medication storage bin. C. All medications are stored in their own prepackaged containers. D. Once medications are opened, they are all kept in the cart, regardless of the directions on the packaging.

The MA is about to administer a medication, but the resident requests that the MA leave the medication on the counter for him or her to take later. What is the correct course of action for the MA? A. Leave the medication as requested by the resident. B. Advise the nurse or supervisor that the resident refused to take the medication. C. Inform the resident that it is against institutional policy to leave the medication, and instruct the resident to call when he or she is ready to take the medication. D. Call the doctor and inform him or her that the resident is refusing to take the prescribed medication.
All of the following are types of oral medications except for __________. A. Powders B. Lotions C. Syrups D. Coated tablets
All of the following are topical medications except __________. A. Ointments B. Foams C. Gels D. Syrups
When a medication is ordered to be given sublingually, how is it given? A. By mouth B. Placed in the cheek C. Placed under the tongue D. Instilled in the nasal cavity
When a medication is ordered to be given in the buccal cavity, how is it given? A. By mouth B. Placed in the cheek “pocket” C. Placed under the tongue D. Instilled in the nasal cavity
When a medication is ordered to be given PO, how is it given? A. By mouth B. Placed in the cheek C. Placed under the tongue D. Instilled in the nasal cavity
When patients are taking metronidazole (Flagyl), which of the following should they avoid? A. Fatty foods B. Sweetened beverages C. Alcoholic beverages D. Salty foods
What is the most common side effect of the diabetic drug metformin? A. Low blood sugar B. Diarrhea C. Sleepiness D. Change in pH
A medication is given for anxiety but causes the resident to become more anxious; this is called a(n) ___________ effect. A. Idiosyncratic B. Paradoxical C. Antagonist D. Agonist
Which of following is not a side effect of phenytoin (Dilantin)? A. Confusion B. Hyperactivity C. Sleepiness D. Rash
What is known as the reaction to antihyperglycemic medication that causes a person to shake and feel nervous? A. Hyperglycemia B. Hypothyroidism C. Hypoglycemia D. Hyperthyroidism
How long should a patient lie flat after you administer a rectal medication? A. 5 to 10 minutes B. 15 to 20 minutes C. 2 to 5 minutes D. 0 to 2 minutes
When giving a patient a histamine blocker, it is important to watch for __________. A. Confusion B. Weakness C. Nausea D. Hallucinations
What is the correct adult dosage for lactulose? A. 1 teaspoon B. 3 teaspoons C. 2 teaspoons D. 1/2 teaspoon
Which of the following is another term for urination? A. Defecation B. Micturation C. Excretion D. Excision

What should a Medication Aide do if he or she is asked by the nurse to give insulin? A. Draw up the correct amount of insulin and administer it as directed. B. Decline the delegation given by the nurse. C. Check the medication administration and prepare the medication for the nurse to administer. D. Make sure that he or she is familiar with the procedure before administering the medication.
